translation.title: Urea Ointment
translation.efficacy: This medicine is used for progressive keratoderma of the fingertips (the dry type of housewife's eczema), keratoderma of the palms and soles, ichthyosis, senile dry skin (senile xerosis), lichen pilaris (keratosis pilaris) and atopic skin.
translation.usage: Wash the affected area, then apply this medicine 1 to several times a day and rub it in thoroughly.
translation.caution: Do not use this medicine if you are hypersensitive to it, on acute eczema or inflammatory skin conditions, if you have kidney failure, or on mucous membranes such as the membranes of the eye. Before using it, consult a doctor or pharmacist if you have inflammation or skin cracks, or if your skin has become more sensitive to irritation. This medicine is for external use only. Do not apply it directly to ulcers, eroded (raw, oozing) areas or wounds. Use it carefully so that it does not touch the eyes, nose, mouth or other mucous membranes. If it accidentally gets into the eyes, rinse them out completely with plenty of water. When using it together with corticoids, dithranol or 5-fluorouracil, consult a doctor or pharmacist. Pain, a feeling of heat, and occasionally flushing and itching may occur. Stop use immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist if adverse reactions occur, such as hypersensitivity symptoms, occasional eczema formation, skin cracks, papules (small bumps), a prickling feeling, a burning feeling or scaling, and rarely swelling or dryness.
